clue.text: Vacillating old barrister steps back in line

indicators.note: stepping back means moving in the opposite direction, so the barrister's letters run the other way
in places one set of letters inside the word that follows

blocks.note: a file is a line of people, as in single file
King's Counsel, the title senior barristers held under a king, before the QC era

explanation.surface: A dithering veteran lawyer shuffles back into the queue.
explanation.walkthrough: KC, not QC, makes the barrister old: senior counsel took the K title under a king. A file is a line, as in single file.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fickle keeps changing their mind, which is what vacillating describes.

clue.text: Hold back in favour of speculator

blocks.note: a bear speculates on prices falling

explanation.surface: Restraint is urged in support of a stock market gambler.
explanation.definitionFit: To forbear is to refrain or restrain oneself from doing something.

clue.text: Absurd award received by top commander

indicators.note: something received is taken in, so the award goes inside

blocks.note: Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A ridiculous medal is handed to the army chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Comic means funny or laughable, close in sense to absurd.

clue.text: Supporters requiring another style of delivery

blocks.note: legs support a table or a body
pin is slang for a leg, so another supporter

explanation.surface: Props needing a different way of being handed over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' is a cricket bowl, not a handover; leg spin is a type of slow bowling that turns the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, leg spin is a kind of bowling, and each bowl is called a delivery.

clue.text: Dismay as a politician interrupts gang of thieves

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: a den of thieves is their hideout, standing for the gang here

explanation.surface: Alarm spreads when an MP bursts in on a band of robbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dismay' reads as a noun in the surface but works as a verb, to discourage.
explanation.definitionFit: To dampen spirits is to discourage or deflate them, a verb sense of dismay.

clue.text: Snappy sailor exercises after game

explanation.surface: A curt seaman works out after a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' is rugby union by its usual initials, a common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An abrupt or snappy manner is curt and short with people.

clue.text: Puppet, one Chopin & Co produced

indicators.note: produced suggests something made up from raw material, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A marionette made by the composer and his associates.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinocchio is the wooden puppet in Collodi's story whose nose grows when he lies.

clue.text: Least sensitive miners' group coming out first?

blocks.note: to come out first is to finish best

explanation.surface: The hardest-bitten mining union winning the vote.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUM was the British miners' trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbest is the superlative of numb, meaning having least feeling.

clue.text: Too likely update on patient's condition?

annotation.answer: AS WELL AS CAN BE EXPECTED

blocks.note: likely means what one would anticipate

explanation.surface: A doctor's cautious report that a patient is probably doing fine.
explanation.walkthrough: Two phrases are joined: 'as well' for too and 'as can be expected' for likely. The question mark flags the stock hospital bulletin.
explanation.definitionFit: Hospitals traditionally describe a patient's state with this guarded set phrase in bulletins.

clue.text: Forbidding religious teaching within borders of Gotham

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its edge letters, its first and last
within puts the teaching inside the outer letters

blocks.note: first and last letters of Gotham

explanation.surface: Batman's city looks bleak when sermons are preached in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A grim or forbidding look is stern and unwelcoming; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Zürich financier consuming exotic roast?

indicators.note: exotic means foreign and strange, so the letters come out in an unfamiliar order
consuming means swallowing, so the financier wraps round the other letters

blocks.note: the gnomes of Zurich are a nickname for Swiss bankers

explanation.surface: A Swiss banker tucks into some unusual roast meat.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged roast goes after the G of GNOME. The whole clue also describes the answer: a food lover eating something exotic.
explanation.definitionFit: A gastronome is a connoisseur of good food, just the person to relish an exotic roast.

clue.text: Awfully cute PA making little contribution to service

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so the letters are put in a wrong order

explanation.surface: A sweet personal assistant does a small bit of work for the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' here is a tea service, a matching set of crockery, not work.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacup is one small piece of a tea service, the crockery set.

clue.text: See 8
Showy type gets tedious work on carriage

blocks.note: a drag is a tiresome chore
a fly is a light one-horse carriage of old

explanation.surface: A flamboyant person is stuck with dull work in a coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Showy type' seems to be a person, but it is the brightly coloured insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Dragonflies are conspicuous insects with bright, iridescent bodies and wings, so showy fits.

clue.text: Inexperienced Othello sent up here, possibly

definitions.text: Inexperienced Othello sent up here, possibly

indicators.note: in a down clue sent up means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: Othello is the Moor of Venice

explanation.surface: A novice actor playing Othello waits nervously backstage.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the place: a nervous new Othello would wait there before going on.
explanation.definitionFit: A green room is the backstage lounge where actors wait before going on stage.

clue.text: Attempt a field event

blocks.note: first meaning: a try, as in having a go
second meaning: the ... put in athletics

explanation.surface: Having a go at an athletics discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot is a try at something, and also the heavy ball thrown in the shot put field event.

clue.text: Retreating rat almost killed

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
retreating means going backwards, so the letters are read right to left

blocks.note: to welsh is to rat, to go back on a promise

explanation.surface: A fleeing rodent was nearly done for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rat' looks like the animal but is the verb; its synonym loses its last letter and is turned around.
explanation.definitionFit: Slew is the past tense of slay, so it means killed.

clue.text: Cooler cocktail

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooler' looks like a chilled drink to go with cocktail, but both are slang for jail and a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Slammer and cooler are both slang for prison, and a tequila slammer is a mixed drink.

clue.text: Fair tennis player overcomes learner in tie

indicators.note: to overcome is to come over, so the tennis player covers what follows
in places the learner inside the tie

blocks.note: L for learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A sporting tennis star beats a novice in a tie-break.
explanation.walkthrough: Two insertions nest: the learner first goes into the tie, then the tennis player wraps round the result. Arthur Ashe won Wimbledon in 1975.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash blonde is a pale greyish-blond hair colour, so a fair shade.

clue.text: Bird or part bird

explanation.surface: A bird, or a portion of one.
explanation.definitionFit: The bittern is a wading bird of the heron family, famous for its booming call.

clue.text: Weed deprived of water can just be hung up

blocks.note: a weed or a drip is a feeble person

explanation.surface: A garden weed lacking water can only hang there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weed' looks like a plant but means a weakling.
explanation.definitionFit: Drip-dry clothing needs no wringing or ironing: you simply hang it up wet.

clue.text: Conservative Right about to come a cropper? Not so far

indicators.note: about means around, so the outer letters wrap round the phrase that follows

blocks.note: to come a cropper is to fail

explanation.surface: A Tory right-winger about to fall flat, but not just yet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come a cropper' is British slang for to fall or fail badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Closer is the comparative of close, meaning nearer, so not so far away.

clue.text: Parent in goal unfortunately makes bloomer

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters end up in a muddle

explanation.surface: A parent playing goalkeeper badly drops a howler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder, but it is something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: The magnolia is a flowering tree, so a bloomer in the literal sense.

clue.text: It's a bizarre case for returning doctor …

definitions.text: It's a bizarre case for returning doctor

indicators.note: bizarre means weird, so the letters are put in an odd order
returning means coming back, so the abbreviation runs backwards
a case holds something inside, so the rearranged letters wrap round

blocks.note: the letters of its a rearranged

explanation.surface: A strange box that the Doctor keeps coming back to.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: Doctor Who's time machine, the police box he travels and returns in. The ellipsis links to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The TARDIS is the time machine shaped like a blue police box in the BBC series Doctor Who.

clue.text: Recalled familiar hat queen's put on again

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: The queen dons a remembered old hat once more.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the queen's R is put on top of the reversed hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Relit means lit again, as a lamp or fire switched or put on again.

clue.text: … like the long-running TV mission that's not on?

blocks.note: first meaning: the TV series Mission
second meaning: not possible, out of the question

explanation.surface: A TV spy assignment that cannot be done.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from the TARDIS clue, another TV reference.
explanation.definitionFit: The American spy series is titled Mission: Impossible, and 'not on' is an idiom for unachievable.

clue.text: Learner takes on universal party game

explanation.surface: A novice joins in with a party game everyone can play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party game' looks like one phrase, but party is wordplay and game alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludo is a board game played with counters and a die.

clue.text: Observation on target

explanation.surface: A comment that hits the spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark is a comment or observation made in passing.

clue.text: No races in the Bluegrass State — that's awkward

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the state's abbreviation

blocks.note: Kentucky, nicknamed the Bluegrass State, abbreviated KY
the TT, the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorcycle races

explanation.surface: No horse racing in Kentucky would be embarrassing.
explanation.definitionFit: A knotty problem is tangled and difficult, so awkward to deal with.
